SIH 2026 · DRDO Problem Statement 26053

DRISHTI

A LiDAR-based perception system for Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) that sees what every other system misses — ditches, trenches, and overhead hazards.

Dataset RELLIS-3D Off-Road
Sensor Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR
Training 20 Epochs · RTX 2080 Ti
Best mIoU 0.328 (3.6× baseline)

Standard autonomous vehicle systems treat the world as a flat map — occupied or empty. DRISHTI builds a full 3D picture of every cell — ground height, ceiling height, semantic class, observability state, and a physics-derived safe speed limit. Here is exactly how it works, step by step.

1

THE ROBOT SEES WITH LASER PULSES

LiDAR scanning · 130,000 beams/second · 3D point cloud generation

🔴

What the LiDAR does

The Ouster OS1-64 spins 360° and fires 64 laser rings × 2048 beams = 130,000 pulses/second. Each beam travels out, hits something, and bounces back in nanoseconds.

✨

What we get

Every bounced beam tells us the exact (x, y, z) position of what it hit, plus intensity (how reflective the surface is). Together: a 3D cloud of ~130,000 colored dots, 10 times per second.

2

SMART MEMORY — FINE NEARBY, BROAD AT RANGE

Toroidal clipmap · 4 resolution levels · 12MB total · auto-scrolls with vehicle

🔍

Like human vision

Your eyes are sharp in the centre, blurry at the edges — and that's enough. DRISHTI uses 4 nested grids: 5cm squares right next to the vehicle, 40cm squares far away. Total memory: just 12MB.

🔄

It scrolls as you drive

As the vehicle moves, the grid shifts with it — old cells behind scroll out (cleared), new cells ahead scroll in (fresh). No rebuilding. No memory growth. The map is always centred on the vehicle.

3

DETECTING HAZARDS OTHER ROBOTS MISS

Negative obstacles · Overhangs · Observability states · Physics-based detection

⛏️

Ditches (Negative Obstacles)

A ditch has no points inside it — the laser beams fall through. DRISHTI tracks where ground should be. Missing returns where ground is expected = ditch flagged. No other mapping system does this.

🌉

Overhangs (Bridges / Branches)

Each grid cell tracks two height layers — ground and ceiling. If the gap between them is smaller than the vehicle's height (2.5m), the path is blocked overhead. A single height value would miss this entirely.

4

THE FINAL MAP — EVERYTHING THE ROBOT KNOWS

Colour-coded terrain · Observability states · Physics-derived safe speed limit

🗺️

What the colours mean

■ Green = safe, drive freely   ■ Orange = rough, go slow   ■ Red = stop, obstacle or ditch   ■ Purple = overhang   ■ Grey ? = never checked — don't assume safe

⚡

Physics-derived speed limit

The safe speed is calculated from physics — braking distance, reaction time, and the distance to the nearest hazard. For a 2m ditch at 15m away: safe speed = 32 km/h. Not a guess — a formula.

THE FOUR CLAIMS

🏔️

Claim 1

Ground height AND ceiling height per cell — required for bridge/overhang detection

📐

Claim 2

Resolution schedule derived from sensor physics — not manually tuned

❓

Claim 3

No return ≠ free. Grey ? cells are unknown — a fundamentally safer default

🚗

Claim 4

Safe speed computed from physics — braking distance + reaction time + hazard range

Training results: 154 tests passing · Best val mIoU: 0.328 (epoch 16) · 3.6× above majority-class baseline · RTX 2080 Ti · 20 epochs · ~47 min
